import re
PARSE_RE = re.compile(r'({{|}}|{[\s\S]+?})')

# Test various patterns
tests = [
    '{x} {y',   # partial unclosed
    '{x',        # unclosed
    'x}',        # stray close
    '{{x}}',     # escaped braces
    'hello {x} world',
]

for t in tests:
    parts = [p for p in PARSE_RE.split(t) if p]
    print(f'{t!r} -> {parts}')
"

Wait! The PARSE_RE split gives `['{x:{y}', '}']` - the `{x:{y}` part matches FIRST (as a field) and then `}` is left as literal text. So `{x:{y}}` gets split into:
- `{x:{y}` - a field (starts with `{`, ends with `}`)
- `}` - stray closing brace

My validator would see:
1. Part `{x:{y}`: starts with `{`, ends with `}` -> valid field
2. Part `}`: literal text with `}` -> raises ValueError!

But the original library WITHOUT my validator would:
1. Process `{x:{y}` as a field -> `_handle_field('{x:{y}')` -> inner = `x:{y` -> split on `:` -> name = `x`, format = `{y` -> `extract_format('{y')` which would try to use `{` as a format type and fail.

So both with and without my validator, `{x:{y}}` would fail. The error message is just different.
